question: Which one of the following is equal to P(A, B, C) given Boolean random variables A, B and C, and no independence or conditional independence assumptions between any of them?
options: P(A, B | C) * P(C | A, B)
P(A | B) * P(B | C) * P(C)
P(C | A, B) * P(A) * P(B)
P(A, B | C) * P(C)
P(A | B, C) * P(B) * P(C)
P(A | B) * P(B | C) * P(C | A, B)
P(A | B, C) * P(B | A, C) * P(C | A, B)
P(A, B) * P(B, C) * P(C, A)
P(A | B) * P(B | C) * P(C | A)
P(A, B, C | D) * P(D)
model_outputs:
The formula P(A, B, C) represents the joint probability of the event A happening together with B happening and C happening. Therefore, it is the product of the probabilities of these three events occurring individually:
P(A, B, C) = P(A | B, C) * P(B, C)
Therefore, the answer is (G).
